item_markdown:
## Add e2e coverage for admin dashboard

- **Value:** medium
- **Need:** `app/[locale]/admin-dashboard/page.tsx` — the highest-privilege route in the app — has zero automated verification; e2e grep for "admin" returns 0 results across all 3 spec files (`07-product-surface.md`; `04-delivery-operations.md` — e2e dir: `e2e/auth.spec.ts`, `e2e/navigation.spec.ts`, `e2e/kudos.spec.ts`)
- **Benefits:** Catches award management regressions (broken admin gate, corrupted award state) before they reach production; admin paths carry the highest data-integrity risk and are exercised least during development.
- **Proposed solution:** Add `e2e/admin.spec.ts` covering: route guard (unauthenticated → redirect), admin page renders award list, and at least one CRUD action (award status change). Feasible because `lib/auth/mock-auth-context.tsx` already supports setting an admin role — no real backend plumbing needed for the test.
- **Effort hint:** low

### CI/CD · 3 items · max=high · effort=low–medium

item_evidence:
---

- Status: opportunity
- Category: test-coverage
- Observation: No coverage provider is installed and `vitest.config.ts` defines no `coverage` block; there is no `@vitest/coverage-v8` or `@vitest/coverage-istanbul` in `package.json`. No coverage report has ever been generated, so there is no baseline to enforce or track.
- Evidence: `vitest.config.ts` — file has 18 lines, no `coverage` key; `package.json` — `devDependencies` lists only `vitest@^2.1.9` with no coverage provider; discovery `04-delivery-operations.md` — "Coverage file: (none) — no coverage/ directory, no lcov.info, no c8/istanbul config"
- Potential improvement: Add `@vitest/coverage-v8` (zero-config, wraps Node's built-in V8 coverage), add a `coverage` block to `vitest.config.ts` with `provider: "v8"`, `include: ["{lib,components,app}/**"]`, and thresholds (`lines: 70, functions: 70, branches: 60`). Add `"test:coverage": "vitest run --coverage"` to `package.json` scripts. This gives the team a concrete baseline and a gate to enforce.
- Customer-value signal: risk reduction
- Value: medium
- Effort hint: low
- Risk if untouched: No visibility into which paths are exercised. Regressions in business logic (`lib/kudos/`, `lib/auth/`) go undetected until a manual test or production incident surfaces them.

---

- Status: opportunity
- Category: test-coverage
- Observation: All 44 components under `components/` have zero unit or integration tests. This includes high-complexity, high-traffic components: `kudos-board-context.tsx` (216 LOC, 11 consumers), `compose-kudo-form.tsx` (168 LOC), and the entire `compose/` sub-tree (6 files).
- Evidence: `05-scale-complexity.md` — "`components/kudos/kudos-board-context.tsx` — 216 LOC"; `03-architecture-shape.md` — "11 inbound imports" for `kudos-board-context.tsx`; grep of `components/` confirms 0 `*.test.*` or `*.spec.*` files; 44 `.tsx` files found under `components/`
- Potential improvement: Write React Testing Library unit tests (compatible with `vitest.config.ts:11` `environment: "node"` after switching to `environment: "jsdom"`) for `kudos-board-context.tsx` state transitions, `compose-kudo-form.tsx` validation feedback path, and `hero-badge.tsx` rank thresholds. Start with the 3 highest-fan-out components; the pure-function badge logic (`lib/kudos/hero-badge.ts`) already has a unit test (`lib/kudos/__tests__/hero-badge.test.ts`) and can serve as the scaffold pattern.
- Customer-value signal: operational efficiency
- Value: medium
- Effort hint: medium
- Risk if untouched: Refactors to the 11-consumer `kudos-board-context.tsx` (god-file risk noted in `03-architecture-shape.md`) have no safety net; a broken state update silently breaks the kudos board for all employees.

---

- Status: opportunity
- Category: test-coverage
- Observation: `lib/auth/mock-auth-context.tsx` — the sole auth layer driving all UI auth state (imported by 6 files) — has no test file. A regression in `MockAuthProvider` or `useMockAuth` would break login, auth-guard redirects, and the notification bell simultaneously with no automated signal.
- Evidence: `03-architecture-shape.md` — "`lib/auth/mock-auth-context.tsx`: imported by 6 files (`login-form.tsx`, `notification-bell.tsx`, `auth-guard.tsx`, `account-menu.tsx`, `kudos-board-context.tsx`, `app/[locale]/layout.tsx`)"; `ls lib/auth/__tests__/` returns empty (confirmed at runtime); `03-architecture-shape.md` — "Auth layer split: `lib/auth/mock-auth-context.tsx` drives all UI auth state (client-side only)"
- Potential improvement: Add `lib/auth/__tests__/mock-auth-context.test.tsx` covering: (a) `MockAuthProvider` default unauthenticated state, (b) login/logout state transitions, (c) `useMockAuth` throws outside provider. Requires `jsdom` environment for this test file (can be set per-file via `// @vitest-environment jsdom`).
- Customer-value signal: risk reduction
- Value: medium
- Effort hint: low
- Risk if untouched: Any change to the mock auth context (e.g., when real Supabase Auth replaces the mock — `lib/kudos/actions.ts:22` TODO) could silently break auth-dependent UI flows across 6 consumers.

- Status: opportunity
- Category: test-coverage
- Observation: The Playwright suite covers only `chromium` (`Desktop Chrome`). No Firefox, WebKit/Safari, or mobile viewport projects are configured. The app targets all Sun* employees (internal), who may use Safari on macOS/iOS or Firefox.
- Evidence: `playwright.config.ts:16` — `projects: [{ name: "chromium", use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"] } }]`; `08-platform-support.md` — "Browser test target: Chromium only (`Desktop Chrome` device profile) — `playwright.config.ts:16`"; app is i18n-capable (vi/en) suggesting broad employee base
- Potential improvement: Add `webkit` and `firefox` projects to `playwright.config.ts`. For an internal app with ~no public traffic this is a 3-line config change. Also add one mobile viewport (`devices["iPhone 14"]`) to catch responsive breakpoints. This triples e2e coverage breadth for the cost of a config edit and slightly longer CI run.
- Customer-value signal: employee productivity
- Value: low
- Effort hint: low
- Risk if untouched: Safari-specific CSS or JS behavior (e.g., Tailwind v4 custom-property usage, Next.js RSC streaming) breaks for macOS/iOS users and is not caught until manual QA.

Mark it `test.skip` or `test.todo` until real auth lands so the suite stays green, but the test documents the expected contract and fails automatically when the TODO is resolved.

- Value: low
